question: In a 100 m Relay Race, how many athletes have to complete a race?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A 100m relay race is a team event in track and field.
 
• The standard relay team consists of four runners.
 
• Each runner is responsible for completing a 100-meter segment of the 400-meter total distance.
 
• The race involves the passing of a baton from one runner to the next.
 
• The exchange of the baton must occur within a designated exchange zone.
 
• The exchange zone is a 20-meter area marked on the track.
 
• If the baton exchange occurs outside of this zone, the team is disqualified.
 
• The first runner starts from the starting line and runs the first 100 meters.
 
• The second runner receives the baton and runs the next 100 meters.
 
• The third runner then takes the baton and runs their 100-meter leg.
 
• The final runner, the anchor, receives the baton and completes the last 100 meters to the finish line.
 
• The team that crosses the finish line first wins the race.
 
• The 100m relay is a popular and exciting event in track and field competitions.
 
• It requires speed, coordination, and precise baton exchanges.
 
• The timing of the exchanges is crucial for a successful race.
 
• Athletes practice baton exchanges extensively to minimize time loss.
 
• The 4x100m relay is a standard event at major athletic competitions, including the Olympics and World Championships.
 
• The race is a test of both individual speed and team coordination.
 
• Relay races are a popular part of many track and field events.
 
• The 4x100m relay is one of the most exciting races to watch.
 
• The speed of the runners, and the fast exchanges, make for a very exciting race.
